sampleMarkdown.welcomeToTheMarkdownPreviewTypeOnTheLeft:
# Welcome to the Markdown preview

Type on the **left** and watch it render on the *right*. Everything here runs in your browser.

## Try these

- Headings, **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~ and `inline code`
- [Links](https://commonmark.org/help/) open in a new tab
- Drag the divider in the middle to give either side more room

### Task list

- [x] Write some Markdown
- [ ] Turn on **Scroll sync** and scroll either side
- [ ] Switch between light and dark mode

> Blockquotes are handy for callouts and quotes.

### Code

```ts
export function greet(name: string): string {
  return `Hello, ${name}!`
}
```

### Table

| Feature       | Guest | Signed in |
| ------------- | :---: | :-------: |
| Live preview  |   ✓   |     ✓     |
| Scroll sync   |   ✓   |     ✓     |
| Save your files |     |     ✓     |

---

Keep scrolling: once this page is longer than the screen, **Scroll sync** keeps both sides at the same place.

{value0}

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Second brain is software you run yourself. The person who installs and runs a copy (the operator) decides where it runs and is responsible for the data on it. This page describes what the software itself stores and does.

sections.heading: What an account stores
paragraphs: When you create an account the server stores your email address, username, first and last name, and a salted scrypt hash of your password. A phone number and a profile picture are stored only if you add them.
If you sign in with Google, Microsoft or Facebook, the server stores the provider’s account identifier and the email address it reports. It never receives your provider password.

The server also stores your theme and reading size, the Markdown files you save, your Watch progress and list, and your Music likes, play history, playlists and radios. Deleting your account removes all of it.

sections.heading: What stays in your browser
paragraphs: Bookmarks, completed notes, lesson progress, the guest Markdown draft and the last area you used are kept in your browser’s local storage. They are not sent to the server and they do not follow you to another device.

sections.heading: Cookies and third parties
paragraphs: The app sets a sign-in cookie and a request-forgery token. Both are needed to keep you signed in and to protect your account. The sign-in cookie is HttpOnly and expires after 12 hours without use.

The app uses no analytics, advertising or tracking scripts, and it loads its scripts, styles and fonts from the same server. A third party receives data only if you choose to sign in with its provider, or if the operator turns on email delivery or an AI classifier.

sections.heading: Files, media and uploads
paragraphs: Study files and media are read from folders the operator chooses. An upload is held in a private inbox until you approve where it goes. You can discard it instead.

If the operator configures an AI classifier, the file name and the first part of the text of an upload are sent to that service to suggest a category. Nothing is sent when no classifier is configured.

sections.heading: How the data is protected
paragraphs: Passwords are hashed with scrypt and a random salt. Session, verification and reset tokens are stored only as hashes. In production the server requires HTTPS, and sign-in attempts are rate limited.
No system is perfectly secure. Tell the operator if you find a problem.

sections.heading: Your choices
paragraphs: In Settings you can see your active sessions, sign out of all devices, export your account data and delete your account permanently. In My profile you can change your name, phone number, picture and linked providers.
Backups made by the operator may keep a copy of deleted data until they are replaced.

sections.heading: Contact and changes
paragraphs: Questions about a particular library go to the person who runs it. If this policy changes, the date above changes with it.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: By creating an account or using this library you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, do not use it.

sections.heading: Your account
paragraphs: Give accurate details, keep your password to yourself and tell the operator if you think someone else has your account. You are responsible for what happens under your account.

sections.heading: Your content
paragraphs: You keep ownership of what you write and upload. By adding a file you confirm you have the right to use it. Documents in the library are visible to the members of this deployment who are allowed to use it.

sections.heading: Media
paragraphs: Watch and Music play files the operator has placed on the server. Only add media you created, own or are licensed to use. The software does not remove copy protection and must not be used to do so.

sections.heading: What you may not do
paragraphs: Do not try to break or bypass security, read another person’s data, overload the server, or upload unlawful content or malware.

sections.heading: Availability and changes
paragraphs: The library is provided as it is. It may be unavailable, change or stop at any time. Keep your own copy of anything that matters to you.

sections.heading: Warranty and liability
paragraphs: The software and this deployment come without any warranty. To the extent the law allows, the authors and the operator are not liable for loss or damage that results from using them.

sections.heading: Ending your use
paragraphs: You can delete your account at any time in Settings. The operator may disable an account that breaks these terms.
